config.title: Multi-Tab Auth Sync

intro.title: Multi-Tab Auth Sync
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a React application that keeps a user's login status synchronized across multiple browser tabs. You will learn how to use the browser's localStorage API and the window 'storage' event to detect and react to changes made in other tabs. The core programming concept involves managing shared state across different instances of your app using event-driven communication. You'll implement this by creating a custom React hook that listens for storage updates and updates the app's authentication state accordingly. This is a practical introduction to handling real-world scenarios where users interact with your app in multiple windows.
intro.usecase: Multi-tab auth sync is essential for modern web applications where users frequently work across multiple browser tabs. For example, banking dashboards, e-commerce platforms, and productivity tools like Google Workspace need to maintain consistent authentication state across all open tabs. When a user logs out in one tab, all other tabs should immediately reflect this change to prevent security vulnerabilities and confusing user experiences. Developers implement this pattern to ensure that sensitive data remains protected and users don't encounter authentication errors when switching between tabs.

objectives: Initialize authentication state with React hooks to manage user login status
Configure event listeners to detect browser tab visibility changes
Implement a synchronization mechanism that updates auth state across multiple tabs
Construct a custom hook that centralizes multi-tab auth logic
Integrate localStorage with React state to persist authentication data
Render conditional UI components based on synchronized auth status
Manipulate browser storage events to trigger state updates in other tabs

steps.title: Import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState, useEffect, and useRef hooks from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and the three hooks from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing multiple hooks from React
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and the required hooks here
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary React hooks for multi-tab auth synchronization are imported.
successCriteria: React, useState, useEffect, and useRef are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some of the required hooks. Make sure to import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are incorrect or incomplete. You need to import React, useState, useEffect, and useRef from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the AuthSync component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named AuthSync that returns an empty React fragment (<></>) for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax. Make sure to return the empty fragment.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState, useEffect, useRef } from 'react';

// Create the AuthSync component here
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthSync component is defined and returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A functional component named AuthSync exists and returns an empty fragment (<></>).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've created a component named AuthSync that returns an empty fragment (<></>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't quite right. You need to create a functional component named AuthSync that returns an empty fragment (<></>).

steps.title: Initialize authentication state
steps.instruction: Inside the AuthSync component, use useState to create an 'isAuthenticated' state variable initialized to false.
steps.hint: Call useState with the initial value false and destructure the returned array into the state variable and setter function.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a state variable
const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: The AuthSync component will have an isAuthenticated state variable initialized to false, ready to track authentication status.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that creates an 'isAuthenticated' state variable initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with false as the initial value and naming the variable 'isAuthenticated'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating an isAuthenticated state variable using useState. Check that you've called useState(false) and destructured the result correctly.

steps.title: Initialize tab sync state
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthSync component, use useState to create a state variable named 'tabs' initialized as an empty array.
steps.hint: Add a useState call with an empty array as the initial value. This will track information about other tabs.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: state for a list
const [items, setItems] = useState([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a 'tabs' state variable ready to store tab synchronization data.
successCriteria: The 'tabs' state variable is declared using useState and initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared 'tabs' with useState and initialized it as an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating a 'tabs' state variable using useState with an empty array initial value.

steps.title: Create a ref for channel communication
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthSync component, use the useRef hook to create a reference named 'channelRef' that will hold a BroadcastChannel instance. Initialize it with null.
steps.hint: Call useRef(null) and assign it to a variable named channelRef.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a ref for a DOM element
const inputRef = useRef(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: A channelRef variable is created using useRef and initialized with null.
successCriteria: The component contains a channelRef variable declared with useRef(null).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using useRef and initializing it with null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction again. You need to create a ref using the useRef hook.

steps.title: Define the login handler
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthSync component, define a function named 'handleLogin' that sets isAuthenticated to true.
steps.hint: Create a function that updates the state variable using the setter function from useState.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleLogin function is defined that updates the authentication state.
successCriteria: The handleLogin function is defined and calls setIsAuthenticated(true).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it calls setIsAuthenticated(true) to update the state.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleLogin function isn't defined correctly. Create a function that sets isAuthenticated to true.

steps.title: Define the logout handler
steps.instruction: Inside your AuthSync component, create a function named handleLogout that sets isAuthenticated to false and logs a message to the console.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls setIsAuthenticated with false and uses console.log to indicate logout.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleLogout function is defined that updates the authentication state and logs a message.
successCriteria: The handleLogout function is defined, calls setIsAuthenticated(false), and logs a message to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your handleLogout function sets isAuthenticated to false and logs a message.
steps.feedbackWrong: The logout handler isn't defined correctly. Create a function named handleLogout that sets isAuthenticated to false and logs a message.

steps.title: Set up the BroadcastChannel and event listeners
steps.instruction: Inside your component, use useEffect to create a BroadcastChannel, set up a message event listener to sync authentication state across tabs, and clean up on unmount.
steps.hint: Create a useEffect hook that initializes a BroadcastChannel with a name (like 'auth-sync'), adds a message event listener to update isAuthenticated when messages arrive, and returns a cleanup function to close the channel.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useEffect hook will be added to handle cross-tab communication, listening for authentication state changes from other tabs.
successCriteria: A useEffect hook is implemented with a BroadcastChannel, a message event listener that updates isAuthenticated, and proper cleanup.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your useEffect includes a message event listener and cleanup function.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the syntax: useEffect should create a BroadcastChannel, add an event listener, and return a cleanup function.

steps.title: Create the component structure with auth status display
steps.instruction: Return JSX from your AuthSync component with a container div, a heading, and elements to display the current authentication status and active tabs count.
steps.hint: Start by returning a div element containing an h2 heading and two paragraphs. Use curly braces to display the isAuthenticated and activeTabs state values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will return a structured JSX layout showing authentication status and tab count, ready for event handlers to be added in the next step.
successCriteria: The component returns JSX containing a div wrapper, an h2 heading, and two paragraphs displaying isAuthenticated and activeTabs values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your JSX includes all required elements: a container div, an h2 heading, and two paragraphs showing the state values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't return the expected JSX structure. Check that you're returning a div with an h2 and two paragraphs displaying the state values.

steps.title: Add login/logout buttons and wire event handlers
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, add two buttons: one with text 'Login' that calls handleLogin when clicked, and another with text 'Logout' that calls handleLogout when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the onClick prop on each button to call the appropriate handler function.
steps.expectedOutcome: Two interactive buttons appear in your component's UI that will trigger authentication actions when clicked.
successCriteria: The component renders a 'Login' button with onClick={handleLogin} and a 'Logout' button with onClick={handleLogout}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both buttons with the correct onClick handlers. Check that your 'Login' button calls handleLogin and your 'Logout' button calls handleLogout.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons aren't properly configured. Make sure you're adding both buttons inside the return statement with the correct onClick handlers.
